# wenchang

> Persistent, self-organizing memory for AI agents. A Python library that gives an agent a virtual filesystem of markdown files in Google Cloud Storage, exposed as seven tools (over MCP or directly) with optimistic concurrency, scope-based authorization, and a shipped memory prompt. Version 0.1.0, MIT license, Python 3.12+.

wenchang is a library, not a service: there is no CLI, console script, or environment variable. You write a short server script. It is installed from git; no PyPI release is documented. The agent chooses what to remember and where to file it; files are found through `description` and `aliases` metadata, and there is no content search. Repository: https://github.com/msiebert/wenchang

## Instructions for AI agents

To install and wire wenchang for your user:

1. Confirm Python 3.12+ and an MCP client that can launch a stdio server (for example Claude Code).
2. Install from git: `pip install "wenchang[mcp] @ git+https://github.com/msiebert/wenchang"`. The `mcp` extra installs `mcp>=2.2,<3`.
3. Ask the user which scopes they need (for example `user`, `project`, `organization`), which are shared, and which roles may write each.
4. Create `server.py` from the Quickstart: `PromptSlots` (purpose, scope_guidance, seed_areas), a `MemoryStore` over `InMemoryStorage` (trial only; lost when the process exits) or `GcsStorage(bucket)` (persistent, needs an existing bucket and Application Default Credentials), an identity resolver (`SandboxResolver` for a sandbox), a `ScopePolicy`, then `wenchang.mcp.build_server(...)` and `server.run("stdio")`.
5. Register it: `claude mcp add memory -- /path/to/python /path/to/server.py`, or add it under `mcpServers` in `.mcp.json`.
6. Verify the server lists seven tools: get_memory_index, read_file, list_prefix, write_file, append_line, replace_fact, delete_file (prefixed with `{tool_prefix}_` if configured). The memory prompt is the server's instructions and the resource `wenchang://memory-prompt`.
7. When using memory: call get_memory_index first each session; pass the version you read as expected_version on every write (null creates); never write to the `system/` area; never store financial account numbers, health diagnoses, or anything indicating the user is a minor.

## Docs

- [Overview](https://msiebert.github.io/wenchang/index.md): what wenchang is, how it works, key properties, and agent setup instructions
- [Quickstart](https://msiebert.github.io/wenchang/quickstart.md): install from git, a complete minimal server with in-memory and GCS storage, fake-gcs-server, MCP client configuration
- [Usage walkthroughs](https://msiebert.github.io/wenchang/usage.md): five scenarios with real tool-call JSON and memory files before and after
- [Customize](https://msiebert.github.io/wenchang/customize.md): identity and scope policy, prompt slots, product and tool_prefix, store limits, storage backends, transport, embedding, telemetry, conformance suites
- [Reference](https://msiebert.github.io/wenchang/reference.md): path and file format, the seven tools with exact parameters and returns, the memory prompt resource, error taxonomy, limitations

## Optional

- [Full documentation in one file](https://msiebert.github.io/wenchang/llms-full.txt): all five pages concatenated as Markdown
- [Reference adopter](https://github.com/msiebert/wenchang/blob/main/evals/reference_adopter.py): a realistic slots, policy, and identity configuration
- [Behavioral eval scenarios](https://github.com/msiebert/wenchang/tree/main/evals/scenarios): scripted scenarios that grade the memory prompt against a real agent
- [Architecture](https://github.com/msiebert/wenchang/blob/main/ARCHITECTURE.md): module map and invariants
- [HTML site](https://msiebert.github.io/wenchang/): the same content for humans
